messages:
lee_support: @marta FYI customer AcmeCorp reporting intermittent 502/504s from /v1/rerank during their morning batch run, started ~09:18 UTC. p95 latency jumped from ~120ms -> ~3s and then gateway timeouts. attaching initial notes.

marta_sre: can you paste one failing request_id and a minimal sample payload so we can repro? also what SDK version are they on?

lee_support: customer sent this quick curl and says it fails intermittently when they ramp to 50 concurrent workers.
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME..."
 -H "Content-Type: application/json"
 -d '{"query":"find best product","candidates":[{"text":"..."}, ... 1200 items ...] ,"top_k":10}'
```

samir_infra: infra dashboards show rerank-service queue depth spike at 09:19:26, p95 latency jumped to 2.9s, instance CPU at 92% and mem increased. Gateway logs show upstream read timeouts followed by 502s. Looks like backend scoring tasks are blocking longer under heavy candidate_count.

marta_sre: two immediate flags: 1) they are sending ~1200 candidates per request (we doc guideline ~<=1000), 2) per-item payload ~20-40KB so token budget per request is huge -> KV cache and batching behave poorly. Also SDK appears to retry immediately on 5xx with no jitter.

acme_ops: we didn't change anything on our side — same SDK release v2.3.1. Workload spike is a steady QPS increase to 400 for 2 minutes during their job window. Retries are default behavior in our internal client.

lee_support: repro plan I sent to them: 1) run client with concurrency=50 and candidate_count=1200 2) enable SDK retries (default) 3) capture request_ids for failures. they've shared two ids: req_20260317_1 and req_20260317_2

marta_sre: internal logs for req_20260317_1:
```
[09:19:27] rerank_worker: start scoring request=req_20260317_1 items=1200 estimated_tokens=1.2M
[09:19:31] rerank_worker: scoring timed out after 4500ms for request=req_20260317_1
[09:19:32] gateway: upstream read timeout for request=req_20260317_1, returning 502
[09:19:33] router: client retry triggered for req_20260317_1 (no jitter)
```

samir_infra: also saw a retry storm: client retried immediately and many requests piled up, causing queue head-of-line blocking. Autoscaler kicked in but pods came up after the peak. deploy-bot shows scale-up at 09:22 (+4 pods).

nina_runtime: quick mitigation we can ask customer to apply: lower concurrency to 8-10, reduce candidate_count to <=400, enable exponential backoff with jitter. That often removes the retry storm and reduces p95.

lee_support: sent suggested temp config to customer. They asked whether we can change anything server-side.

marta_sre: server-side short-term options: 1) temporarily increase per-request service timeout to 12s for this org (so we don't return 502 while worker finishes), 2) enable per-org circuit breaker to cap concurrent in-flight requests, 3) return 429 earlier when candidate_count exceeds safe token budget. Longer term: patch runtime to cap effective in-flight tokens per worker and emit early 429 with Retry-After if candidate_count > 1000.

nina_runtime: I'll prepare a small runtime change: cap candidate_count at 1000 and return 429 + Retry-After. I can target a patch today for canary. Also add instrumentation to surface "effective_tokens" per request.

samir_infra: for immediate relief I'll widen the burst autoscaling threshold and add a temporary 10s circuit-breaker on the gateway to shed load rather than pile it onto the backend. Taking it slowly so we don't flail.

marta_sre: repro and verification steps for oncall:
- Run load harness: 50 concurrent clients, candidate_count=1200, item size ~25KB each.
- Observe queue depth, p95, and gateway 502s.
- Apply client-side mitigations (concurrency=8, candidate_count=400, backoff) to confirm p95 returns to normal.
- Deploy nina's cap on candidate_count and verify 429 behavior.

lee_support: drafted customer-facing note summarizing actions and asking for time slot to coordinate a joint test at 09:55 UTC. Copying snippet: "We observed retry storms + very large candidate lists causing backend scoring timeouts under load. Please reduce concurrency and enable backoff; we'll push a protective cap on candidate_count and patch runtime monitoring. We'll run a joint test at 09:55 UTC."

acme_ops: ok let's do the joint test at 09:55. we'll also try lowering concurrency on our side now.

marta_sre: action items assigned: samir_infra -> adjust autoscale + gateway CB, nina_runtime -> patch cap+instrumentation, lee_support -> coordinate ACME test and collect request_ids, marta_sre -> monitor canary and confirm no regression.

nina_runtime: file note: will add server-side 429 for candidate_count>1000 and include Retry-After header; small PR queued id=#4721.

lee_support: thanks all. I'll update the thread after the 09:55 joint test and attach failure ids and any new logs.

samir_infra: marking this as HANDOFF -> oncall: please continue monitoring rerank p95 and escalate if spikes reappear.

marta_sre: closing triage for now, keep thread open until post-test confirmation. :thumbsup:
